cast.identity: Nell, the older automaton-maker and landlady: warm medium-brown skin, kind older face, silver-blue hair braided into a bun, round brass spectacles with a fine chain. Teal-green cardigan over a cream collared blouse, canvas BIB work apron with only a small brass screwdriver and open-ended spanner in its pocket, plum work skirt, plum-brown sturdy boots. Match the supplied selected concept. Her short wooden walking stick can be carried in the same near hand in each painted phase, staying inside the cell and with its ferrule no lower than the planted boot. Keep the opposite arm's walk swing and both boot gestures readable.

Mira, a surveyor/map-maker: medium warm brown skin, friendly brown eyes, short wavy espresso bob and two brass hair clips. Plum collared field jacket with pocket flaps and sage turned cuffs, cream shirt, ochre neckerchief, dark olive trousers, chestnut boots and a compact brown map satchel with two short rolled maps. Exact character identity and clothes of the supplied selected concept.

Rowan, the older keeper of the sparkworks: warm skin, brown eyes, silver swept-back hair, thick silver eyebrows and a neatly trimmed silver beard. Brown flat cap, teal waistcoat, cream collarless rolled-sleeve shirt, rust neckerchief, canvas-brown trousers and chestnut boots. A small brass pressure gauge clips securely to his breast pocket, not a floating watch. Exact identity and clothes of the selected concept. Empty hands.

Bram, the carpenter: warm brown skin, expressive brown eyes, full dark-brown curly hair, cheerful friendly face and a pencil tucked behind an ear. Rust-orange knit vest over a burgundy collared rolled-sleeve shirt, a dark brown leather bib carpenter apron with a plain folding wooden ruler in a pocket, dark blue-grey trousers and chestnut work boots. Exact identity and clothes of the selected concept. Empty hands.

Tessa, the orchard keeper: warm fair skin, light freckles, friendly brown eyes and copper-orange hair in a long side braid. Wide straw sun hat with a sage ribbon, sage neckerchief, short rust-red rolled-sleeve work jacket over a cream shirt, olive trousers and chestnut boots. Gardening gloves are tucked securely into her belt. Match the selected concept exactly, especially the broad soft hat and copper braid. Keep the hat inside each cell. Empty hands.

character_se_prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit / production painted-frame character skin.
Input image 1 is the STRICT nine-pose sprite sheet to repaint, defining the exact camera, frame order, gait phases, body scale and layout. Input image 2 is the SELECTED character identity and clothing reference.
Repaint all nine figures of image 1 as this SAME person from image 2. This is a full appearance replacement in the existing animation, not nine new poses or a turnaround.
Canvas: exactly 1254x1254 pixels, 3 columns x 3 rows, nine 418x418 cells; transparent RGBA. Exactly one full body in each cell. Frames 1–8 are the eight walk phases matching image 1 cell for cell; frame 9 at bottom right is a relaxed neutral stand, both feet planted, distinct from the walking poses. Preserve the precise supporting boot, lifted boot sole, stride, arm swing, head direction and body placement of each corresponding pose. Do not reorder or duplicate walk phases.
All figures face front-right / SOUTHEAST, with the same elevated three-quarter camera. Keep the approved painted roughly three-head-tall anatomy, character height, boot size and clear silhouette. Express age through the face and clothing, not different proportions. No realistic adult body or child redesign. Preserve the reference's crisp dark warm-brown outline, painterly shading and warm light. Consistent identity, clothing and accessories in all nine cells; readable large clothing shapes rather than tiny textures. These are game sprites, not a fashion sheet.
Keep every figure entirely inside its own cell with ample transparent gaps, head and feet clear of the cell edges. Truly transparent background, no shadow, no floor, no border, no text or pose numbers. No extra poses, no alternate costumes, no scenery. It must fit the same motion family and mirror correctly without readable lettering.

robots.name: Pip — postal sorter
robots.design: A compact red enamel POST-BOX robot, waist high to a human: softly rounded rectangular body, domed postal-red lid, one large round amber face window in a brass rim, two tiny glowing oval spark-eyes and NO mouth/nose. Below it two simple pigeonhole cubbies hold envelopes; a routine card slot sits under the lid. Two small red mitten hands on short solid arms, one plain canvas satchel attached to its side. The entire body sits DIRECTLY on a small teal rolling chassis with two large rubber wheels and one hidden little caster. No legs, boots, walking struts or floating body. Distinct post-box silhouette, small readable forms. WORK: lift an envelope from a cubby and place it into the open satchel.

robots.name: Trowel — gardener
robots.design: A low rounded watering-can robot in soft mint/cream enamel, two-thirds of a person's height. One round brass-rimmed amber face with two glowing oval eyes, no mouth or nose; a plain spout arm with a perforated rose, a tiny opposite mitten grip, a small seed hopper at the back and just a few tidy leaves near its cap. Its body attaches directly to a broad two-wheel teal chassis with a little rear caster, no legs or feet. Oversized soft rubber wheels handle cobbles. Warm, contented domestic garden tool silhouette; not a human wearing robot clothes. WORK: tilt the spout and water a small potted seedling within the same cell, then return it upright.

robots.name: Wick — lamplighter
robots.design: A taller slim cream-enamel lamplighter, about adult shoulder height, with a small teal pagoda-like lantern cap, ONE brass-rimmed round amber face in the lantern head, two glowing eyes, no human face. Its narrow body mounts directly to a stable rounded cream/teal wheelbase with two FAT rubber wheels and a little caster; no long leg-like posts beneath the body. Short simple arms hold a telescoping brass lighting pole close to the body during rolling. The pole folds short enough to fit the frame. WORK: raise/extend the pole toward a small lamp fitting at the cell edge, touch it to light it, keeping all parts visible and mechanically connected.

robots.name: Heron — yard crane
robots.design: A friendly compact teal yard crane, wider and a little taller than a person. A rounded teal/cream body with ONE large round brass-rimmed amber spark-eye window sits directly on a broad FOUR-WHEEL rubber chassis, no legs or feet. A clean hinged teal boom with brass pivot discs rises from the back, a real cable runs over its tip to a rounded brass hook. Keep the boom compact/folded for travel, visually simple and cute rather than industrial gear clutter. Body, chassis, boom, pivots, cable and hook remain coherent across every view. WORK: smoothly lift one small wooden crate a little above the ground, then settle it down, no enormous crane swinging outside its cell.

robots.name: Tender — maintenance helper
robots.design: A squat tortoise-shaped cream-and-teal maintenance robot, knee high, with a broad soft dome shell, one large round brass-rimmed amber spark-face with two glowing oval eyes, and two short folding mitten arms curled beside its front. Four small rubber wheels tuck into a low teal chassis attached directly under the body. A small neat moss patch grows at the rear seam; otherwise cared for and friendly. A discreet routine slot and rear service hatch. No legs, insect appendages or scary exposed machinery. WORK: open a small inspection cover on a short pipe segment and gently turn a reachable valve with one mitten, then tuck the arm away.

robots.name: Tally — trading assistant
robots.design: A new small friendly merchant's assistant in cream enamel with muted ochre and deep teal accents, roughly waist high. Soft rounded-rectangle body like an old shop cashbox, one large circular brass-rimmed amber spark-face with two simple glowing oval eyes, no mouth/nose. A shallow securely attached counting tray at the front, a narrow receipt/routine slot, two stubby mitten arms, and a small till drawer low in the body. The body mounts DIRECTLY on two broad rubber wheels and a small rear caster. A few large simple coin discs, no written prices or currency branding. WORK: count/place one coin onto the tray, offer a short receipt, then return to the neutral travelling pose. Simple charming municipal machine, not a humanoid bank clerk.

robot_prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept, production-oriented robot sprite/motion reference sheet.
Asset type: ONE transparent RGBA 1536x1024 sheet, EXACTLY FOUR COLUMNS and THREE ROWS of equal cells. Input image is the approved wheeled automaton family; borrow its family language and warm painted outlines, but draw ONLY the specified individual design consistently twelve times.
ROW 1: four clear neutral TURNAROUND views in order southeast/front-right, southwest/front-left, northeast/back-right, northwest/back-left. Show the genuine back with rear panels, not a face on its back.
ROW 2: four successive SE-facing ROLLING phases. Keep the same stable body, scale and camera; motion is wheel rotation, a very small soft body settle, gentle arm/tool response. Wheel spokes progress through four quarter-turn positions. These are not walking poses; wheels remain in contact with a common baseline.
ROW 3, all SE-facing: OFF (dim face eyes), IDLE (warm eyes), WORK START, WORK END. The two work poses show the simple job described below. Give distinct useful work states, mechanically attached limbs/tools and fixed wheel contacts.
Style: simplified rounded enamel shapes, cream/teal family accents, restrained brass rims and hubs, dark warm-brown outlines, softly painted shading like the provided family sheet, crisp at small game scale. Every robot has one round spark window; no mouth/nose or human face. Ground motion uses wheels with visible axles/hubs and a directly supported body, NEVER legs or shoes.
All twelve bodies must be the same character, same apparent size and wheel/tool design in their own cells. Leave roomy transparent gaps and fit the complete robot plus its tool within every cell. No ground shadows, background, scenery, grid lines, labels, lettering or pose numbers. The whole image has a genuinely transparent background; no paper or checkerboard. No duplicate family members, no Hotaru or humans.
